subject: Re: HelixBank security questionnaire follow-up — RBAC granularity, audit evidence, separation of duties
body:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@helixbank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@helixbank.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 3, 2025 at 2:18 PM PT
Subject: HelixBank security questionnaire follow-up — RBAC granularity, audit evidence, separation of duties

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re finalizing the “Access Controls / Authorization” section of our vendor security questionnaire and need a few additional details specific to RBAC.

Could you please confirm/provide:

1) Fine-grained roles
- Do you support roles beyond “admin/user”? (e.g., Billing Admin vs Security Admin vs Developer vs Read-only)
- Can roles be applied at different scopes (org vs project vs environment)?

2) Separation of duties
- Can a Billing Admin be restricted from modifying SSO/SAML settings?
- Can a Security Admin be restricted from viewing billing/payment details?
- Can audit log export be restricted to Security Admin (not Org Admin)?

3) Audit evidence
- Do audit logs include: actor identity, role, permission evaluated, allow/deny decision, timestamp, source IP?
- Can you provide a sample event (redacted) showing an authorization decision for a sensitive action (e.g., API key rotation / org settings update)?

4) Support / break-glass
- Do Redwood support staff ever impersonate customer users?
- If yes: is it time-bounded, approval-based, and logged? Can customers disable it?

If it’s easier, you can respond inline in this thread. We can also accept a short doc + sample log event as attachments.

Best,
Nina

—
Nina Patel
Third Party Risk Management
HelixBank



From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@helixbank.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@helixbank.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 4, 2025 at 10:06 AM PT
Subject: Re: HelixBank security questionnaire follow-up — RBAC granularity, audit evidence, separation of duties

Hi Nina,

Absolutely — thanks for the clear list. I’m looping in Olga (GRC) and Kevin (Audit Logging) to make sure we cover the evidence/audit portions precisely.

Inline responses below, and I’m attaching (1) our RBAC v2 overview and (2) the default role matrix we’re using as the enterprise baseline.

Attachments:
- Redwood_RBAC_v2_Overview_Feb2025.pdf
- Redwood_RBAC_v2_Default_Roles_Matrix_v0.1.xlsx

1) Fine-grained roles
- Yes. We are in the process of rolling out “RBAC v2”, moving from coarse feature gating to explicit resource/action permissions.
- Default roles include: Org Admin, Billing Admin, Security Admin, Developer, Read-only, and Support/Impersonation (internal-only, tightly controlled).
- Scopes: today we support org-level roles. RBAC v2 adds consistent scoping across org + project (and for Private deployments, scoped to the customer’s tenant boundary). We can share the specific scope model in the attached overview.

2) Separation of duties
- Yes, separation-of-duties is a core requirement driving this redesign.
- Billing Admin vs SSO/SAML: supported as separate permission sets (Billing Admin does not get IdP/SSO config by default).
- Security Admin vs billing: Security Admin does not receive billing/payment permissions by default.
- Audit log export: we agree this should be a Security Admin capability and not implicitly granted. Our current default matrix reflects that direction; we can also provide a “least privilege” recommended setup for your admins.

3) Audit evidence
- Audit logs include actor identity, org/project context, timestamp, and source metadata. RBAC v2 adds explicit authorization decision context (permission evaluated, allow/deny, policy version, and reason code).
- Kevin can provide a redacted sample event for a sensitive operation.

4) Support / break-glass
- Support impersonation (where enabled) is time-bounded and approval-based, and creates explicit audit events.
- For Private deployments, customers can disable support impersonation entirely.
- For Hosted/Dedicated, support access is constrained and heavily audited; break-glass elevation is separate from standard support access and requires additional approvals.

If helpful, we can do a 30-min working session with your security team to map your questionnaire fields directly to our artifacts.

Best,
Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Marcus — thank you (attachments received).

Two quick follow-ups:

A) Audit log sample
Could you send one sample audit event showing an authZ decision for a sensitive action (redacted is fine). The questionnaire specifically asks for “authorization decision logging”.

B) Audit log export permission
You mentioned you agree export should be restricted to Security Admin. Can you confirm whether Org Admin can export audit logs by default today, and whether that changes in RBAC v2 defaults?

Thanks,

From: Kevin Osei <kevin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@helixbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@helixbank.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 6, 2025 at 11:23 AM PT
Subject: Re: HelixBank security questionnaire follow-up — RBAC granularity, audit evidence, separation of duties

Hi Nina,

Jumping in on the audit evidence pieces.

A) Sample audit event (authZ decision)
Attached is a redacted sample event in text form: Audit_Log_Sample_AuthZ_Decision_Event.json.txt

It demonstrates:
- actor (user id + email)
- role ids (resolved at time of decision)
- permission/action evaluated
- resource + scope context
- decision allow/deny
- reason code
- policy bundle version
- request metadata (source IP, user agent)

Note: the exact field names can vary slightly between surfaces (Hosted control plane vs Console), but the semantics are consistent and we maintain schema versioning for downstream SIEM ingestion.

B) Who can export audit logs
- Historically, Org Admin could access most “org settings” including audit log export.
- Under RBAC v2 defaults, export is being moved into Security Admin (and a narrower “Audit Log Viewer/Exporter” permission set). Org Admin is not intended to implicitly include export going forward.

If you want, I can provide a second sample event showing a *deny* decision (e.g., Billing Admin attempting to export audit logs) since some questionnaires ask specifically for denied actions to be logged.

Regards,
Kevin

—
Kevin Osei
Audit Logging / Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Nina,

Adding a couple notes from the compliance/evidence angle (for your questionnaire package):

- Evidence artifacts we typically provide for RBAC/audit controls:
  1) RBAC role definitions + permission mapping (default roles)
  2) Sample audit log events (allowed + denied)
  3) Control narrative describing approval/monitoring for elevated access (break-glass)

- Support/break-glass:
  We treat support impersonation and break-glass elevation as separate controls. Both generate explicit audit events. Break-glass is time-bounded, approval-based, and monitored.

- If you need SOC 2 mapping language for your internal controls, we can provide a short control narrative plus references to our SOC 2 report under NDA (separately from this email thread).

Let us know the specific questionnaire control IDs you’re working against (if they have them); we can align wording to reduce back-and-forth.

Best,
Olga

1) How RBAC policies/role definitions are distributed/updated in Private (esp. if air-gapped)
2) Whether support impersonation can be fully disabled for Private
3) Whether customers can require approvals for any elevated access workflow (i.e., no unilateral Redwood action)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@helixbank.com>
Cc: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@helixbank.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 4:42 PM PT
Subject: Re: HelixBank security questionnaire follow-up — RBAC granularity, audit evidence, separation of duties

Hi Nina,

Confirmed — for Private deployments (including air-gapped), the model is explicitly designed around customer-controlled distribution and customer-controlled support posture.

1) RBAC policy distribution/updates (Private / air-gapped)
- RBAC v2 policies are packaged as a versioned “policy bundle” artifact.
- For Private, bundles are delivered as part of the installer/upgrade process (and can be transported offline). We sign the bundle artifact and validate signature at install/upgrade time.
- We handle version skew by pinning the policy bundle version to the deployed control plane version (and logging the active policy version in audit events).

2) Support impersonation can be disabled (Private)
- Yes. Private customers can disable support impersonation entirely. If disabled, Redwood has no impersonation path into your tenant.

3) Customer-required approvals for elevated access
- Yes. Elevated access (break-glass) is time-bounded and approval-based, and we can align the approver workflow to your requirements for Private (e.g., require explicit customer approval / ticket reference before any elevated session is activated).
- Regardless, we emit dedicated audit events for elevation start/stop, including who approved, duration, and the rationale/ticket reference.

If you’d like, we can provide a short “Private support posture” one-pager tailored to HelixBank’s questionnaire language (Olga can help align this to your control framework).

Best,
Marcus

—
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
